Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@zerosync.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: cost/perf tuning help for inference rollout

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the demo earlier. We’re lining up a limited rollout of Redwood for our customer facing summarization endpoint and I wanted to get alignment on the cost/perf checklist before we kick off implementation. High-level: we need steady throughput during peak batches (~300 req/min), keep 95th latency under 350ms, and keep monthly token spend below our SLO.

Key concerns from our infra/finance teams:
- Tail latency spikes when traffic bursts hit concurrent sessions (we use long context, avg 1.2k tokens)
- We saw quality drops after aggressive quantization in a POC; need guidance on quant profile selection and evals
- Want a routing policy that falls back gracefully to cheaper variants for non-critical calls

Can you share a pragmatic plan (who does what, telemetry to collect, suggested quant profiles to try first, and a proposed batching/caching config) so we can schedule implementation work with our SREs next week?

Appreciate it — I can loop in our procurement contact if we need to discuss capacity or quotes.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Infrastructure, ZeroSync

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the clear context. We can definitely help get a targeted implementation plan together. Proposed next steps:

1) Kickoff call (30m) — run through constraints, SLOs, and sample traffic. Owner: Ava.
2) Baseline telemetry capture (48–72h) — collect P50/P95/P99, request size distribution, KV cache hit rates. Owner: ZeroSync SRE + Redwood instrumentation guide (we’ll provide a short snippet).
3) Quantization profiles trial — start with fp16 -> Q4_0 (sensitivity checks) -> int8 if quality stable. Owner: Redwood/Monica to produce recommended eval prompts.
4) Batching & latency policy — suggested initial max_batch_size=8, max_wait=20ms, adaptive batch window enabled. Measurement target: P95 <= 350ms.
5) Caching & prefetch — enable prefix + KV cache; set TTL=60s for session cache initially, iterate based on hit rate.
6) Routing policy — primary model is gpt-like-highperf; fallback to gpt-like-cost (cheaper quantized variant) for non-interactive endpoints. Implement gradual rollout/canary.

I’ve attached a short kickoff agenda (warmup_agenda.pdf). I’m looping in Monica for the implementation checklist and an owner-level plan for the trial quant profiles. Rishi — flag if we need to push pricing or quota details up front.

Can we schedule the kickoff early next week? My availability: Mon/Tue 9–11am PT.

Thanks,
Ava Chen

Hi Samira / Ava —

Appreciate the brief. I put together a compact implementation playbook below so your SREs and engineers have clear checkpoints. I’m calling this a \"warm-up\" because the goal is to move from POC -> predictable run in two sprints (2 weeks).

Warm-up implementation playbook (owner in parentheses):
A) Baseline capture (ZeroSync SRE + Redwood instrumentation) — 72h
   - Capture: request size histogram, seq length, tokens per response, latency P50/P95/P99, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization. (Owner: ZeroSync)
   - Redwood provides a small telemetry snippet and a dashboard template. (Owner: Monica)

B) Controlled quant experiments (Redwood + ZeroSync) — 3 days per profile
   - Profiles: fp16 (baseline) -> Q4_0 (lower mem, mixed results historically) -> int8 (aggressive; require eval).
   - Eval: run ~200 prompt set (representative) and calculate accuracy/regression delta vs fp16. Abort if regression > 1.5% on key metrics. (Owner: Monica)
   - Deliverable: short report with pass/fail per profile and recommended profile for staging.

C) Batching & adaptive window tuning (ZeroSync + Redwood) — ongoing
   - Start: max_batch_size=8, max_wait_ms=20, allow dynamic window expansion under low-latency SLO.
   - Run load test: synthetic burst and 95th latency check. If P95 > 350ms, decrease batch size or lower max_wait. (Owner: Karthik / ZeroSync SRE)

D) Caching strategy (ZeroSync + Redwood)
   - Enable prefix caching and KV cache. Initial TTL 60s for session cache; measure hit rate. If hit rate > 30% consider raising TTL. (Owner: ZeroSync)

E) Routing & fallback policy (Redwood)
   - Route production traffic to verified-highperf model. Non-critical/async calls route to cost-optimized quantized variant.
   - Implement rollout policy: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with failure thresholds (error rate, latency). (Owner: Monica / Rishi)

F) SLO verification & cost guardrails (joint)
   - Set alerts for P95 latency, error rate, and token spend per hour. Configure automatic rollback to previous model variant if thresholds crossed. (Owner: ZeroSync + Redwood)

Timeline proposal:
- Week 1: Baseline capture + small synthetic load tests
- Week 2: Quant experiments + initial batch tuning + enable caching in staging
- Week 3: Canary routing + monitor; finalize quant profile for production

Deliverables attached: implementation-checklist.csv (checklist of tasks + owners) and a short shared doc for the prompt set (link below).

Questions / immediate asks:
- Please confirm who from your SRE team will own baseline capture and provide access to a staging endpoint.
- We recommend freezing the core prompt set for quant evals (we can share an initial 200 examples).

Link to shared playbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cWarmupPlan

I’ll be available Monday for the kickoff at 9:30am PT—Ava, can you confirm?

Regards,
Monica Patel
